ideas.pitch: An AI-powered smart garbage classifier using low-cost hardware and computer vision to optimize local municipal waste collection routes.
ideas.title: IoT Smart Dustbin and Waste Analytics Platform
ideas.why_it_could_win: Follows the winning pattern from TechnoMorph Hackathon by featuring a working computer vision waste classifier integrated with hardware simulations, appealing directly to the IoT and CSE background of the hosting department.

ideas.pitch: A hyper-local civic tech app that drives foot traffic to local businesses through GPS-verified check-ins paired with an automated AI marketing copy generator.
ideas.title: LocalShops AI Walk-to-Earn & Copilot
ideas.why_it_could_win: Mimics the 1st place winner at Chatswood AI Real-World Impact Hackathon by combining a tangible real-world local economic benefit with a live dashboard that judges can test instantly on their mobile browsers.

ideas.pitch: An IoT dashboard tracking real-time power consumption across departmental lab nodes, using lightweight anomaly detection to flag electrical faults instantly.
ideas.title: Campus Smart Energy & IoT Anomaly Monitor
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly targets the host institution's Department of CSE (IoT, CS & BT) by solving a relatable campus-level infrastructure problem within a tight 8-hour window.

ideas.pitch: A lightweight voice assistant extension that analyzes incoming phone and browser audio streams in real-time to alert users about common phishing and financial scams.
ideas.title: Voice-First Senior Fraud Shield
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the winning architecture of the GOSIM Agentic Hackathon by delivering a voice-first protective agent that solves an immediate, highly emotional social problem with high demo impact.

ideas.pitch: An AI agent that automatically logs, categorizes, and proposes verified pull requests or maintenance tickets for reported campus software and hardware bugs.
ideas.title: Autonomous Campus Incident Response Agent
ideas.why_it_could_win: Replicates the grand prize-winning data agent concept from the DataHub Agent Hackathon by demonstrating a fully closed-loop autonomous repair workflow rather than just a conversational wrapper.
